newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK&China Gas results in line - analysts.
newsitem.headline: HK&China Gas results in line - analysts.

text.p: The interim results of blue chip Hong Kong and China Gas, showing a 20 percent rise in net profit, were slightly better than market expectations, analysts said on Tuesday.
"The results are better than our full year forecast of 18.3 percent for 1996," said Marvin Lo, investment analyst at Amsteel Research (H.K.) Ltd.
The company reported earnings of HK$979.1 million, compared with HK$815.4 million in first half 1995. Turnover rose at a slower rate of 12.1 percent to HK$2,494.4 million.
"I was looking for (net profit growth of) 16.3 percent... so I am revising up," said Elvic Ng, research analyst at Vickers Ballas.

Analysts said that while five-year average earnings growth for the utility has fallen to about 20 percent from 30 percent in the 1980s, it is still the best buy in the sector in terms of earnings growth.
"Earnings growth for the company is dependent on population growth," said Lo.
Consumption per metre, that is per household, has shown very low to zero growth in recent years, analysts said.

Amsteel is forecasting an average seven percent to eight percent growth in sales volume plus a four to five percent rise in gas charges to yield 18.3 percent growth in earnings in 1996 and 19.9 percent growth in 1997.
Despite the company's high price, analysts continue to recommend a buy for Gas.
"The share is trading on a high PER (price earnings ratio), but it is the only utility not regulated (by a government scheme of control) and there are no negative factors in its outlook," said Lo.
The share shed HK$0.05 to close at HK$12.80.
